doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Mistakes in improvising and the middle school students
summary: Mistakes are heard and self-corrected, illustrated by a student at Park Middle School hitting a major third over a minor chord.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Are there mistakes in improvising for you?
Yes. That’s when the kids that I’m working with up at Park Middle School in Jeffersonville about five miles from my house — every morning from nine to nine forty- © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

five — I’ve been working with them for two months. Free, just to do it. Eight saxophones. Yes there are mistakes. And today Sebastian, he’s playing his tenor and he goes [scats] I put on Volume 24, major and minor. We work with major, the B flat major scale. Today we worked with the B flat concert minor scale. We practiced the scale, practiced the arpeggio up to the ninth and back down. They couldn’t have done this two months ago at all, not at all. Anyhow, when he was playing he went up and hit the major third, his C minor. He his an E but when he hit it he went — his eyes blinked and he lowered it a half step. And I stopped — I let him play it for a few seconds and then I stopped and I said, “Did everybody hear that?” And a couple of them, yeah. I said, “He’s self-correcting himself.” He hit a major third against a minor chord, which is one of the worst things for your ears to hear. But he heard it, and he wouldn’t have heard it two months ago when we started. So I relax when Sebastian is playing because he can self correct. That’s the way we all want to be. So that means you have to listen to what you’re playing in relation to the CD that I brought in and the little speaker. So yes there are mistakes but not the kind you’re talking about I don’t think.
